name: Javan
title: Ancestor of the Greek peoples
summary: Javan was the son of Japheth and grandson of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Greek and Ionian peoples. In the biblical table of nations in Genesis 10, he is linked to groups around the Mediterranean, and his name is used prophetically for Greece in later writings.

keyEvents.title: The Birth and Lineage of Javan
keyEvents.description: Javan is mentioned as a son of Japheth in the genealogy after the flood, where Noah's descendants spread across the earth.

keyEvents.title: The Sons of Javan and the Peoples
keyEvents.description: Javan's four sons—Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim—are linked to various peoples and coastal regions around the Mediterranean Sea.

keyEvents.title: The Dispersion of Nations from Javan
keyEvents.description: From Javan's descendants, the coastal peoples spread into their own territories, each with its own language and clans.

keyEvents.title: Javan as a Trading Partner with Tyre
keyEvents.description: The prophet Ezekiel mentions Javan (Greece) as traders who engaged in exchange with Tyre, including people and bronze goods.

keyEvents.title: Javan in Isaiah's Prophecy
keyEvents.description: Isaiah prophesies about God's glory being proclaimed among distant nations, and Javan is mentioned as one of these peoples.

keyEvents.title: Javan in the Prophecies of Daniel and Zechariah
keyEvents.description: In Daniel's vision, Javan (Greece) represents a powerful kingdom that will defeat Persia. Zechariah prophesies about God's victory over the sons of Javan.
